locator: §4.1, 'Schroeder (2008b, 2008c) dubs the distinction between inconsistencies that involve one attitude-type directed towards inconsistent contents, A-type inconsistencies'
interpretation: Schroeder's cost argument as the entry reports it, developed through Hare's phrastic/neustic model: once moral and non-moral judgments differ by attitude type, complex sentences 'express attitudes that don't reduce to the attitudes which would be expressed by either conjunct', so new attitude types and rules are needed, and inconsistency has to be explained by incoherence between attitude types (B-type); the clearest genuine inconsistencies are A-type, a reason to prefer an A-type model if non-cognitivists could build one. Read as a cost of that architecture of the logic of attitudes, not of expressivism as such (Codex P1 on #187): it is recorded as an attack on Blackburn's logic-of-attitudes explanation of validity, and leaves A-type replies open. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
